Subject: Calyx DR requirements: RTO/RPO targets and regional continuity

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As Calyx moves toward production for our fraud-modeling pipeline we need to lock down acceptable RTO/RPO targets and understand how Redwood will handle region-to-region activation. A few specific asks from our side: 

- Target RTO for primary region failover: 30 minutes from detection to traffic failover (we know this is aggressive).
- Target RPO: 15 minutes maximum for customer transactions.
- Clarify whether active-passive or active-active approaches are supported for multi-region model serving and what warm/cold cache assumptions imply for latency during failover.
- We also need a statement on SLA credits/termination rights if the platform misses regional continuity commitments for >3 events in a quarter.

I've attached our DR questionnaire (summary) so you can see the fields procurement will focus on. We appreciate any mitigation levers (reserved capacity, pre-warm, cross-region replication) and rough cost delta for stronger guarantees.

Can we get a written proposal that calls out feasible commitments and the tradeoffs? Procurement will want numbers to bake into the contract.

Best,
Samir

Subject: Re: Calyx DR requirements: RTO/RPO targets and regional continuity

Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. High level response up front: we can meet Calyx's objectives with an explicit addendum, but the 30m RTO / 15m RPO targets will require a combination of reserved capacity in both regions and a tighter replication cadence than our default. That has an operational and pricing impact.

Key points (summary):
- Feasible option A (High-availability): active-passive with pre-warmed secondary. Typical cold-start components (model load time + kv-cache rebuild) can be reduced via pre-warm; estimated activation RTO: 20–40 minutes depending on model size. RPO: down to 15 minutes if we enable continuous cross-region replication for model state and persistent logs (this requires a data-replication connector from Calyx or use of our streaming sync add-on).
- Option B (Economical): active-passive with on-demand warm-up. RTO: 45–90 minutes. RPO: 1 hour. Lower cost but slower recovery and transient latency spikes during failover.
- Option C (Active-active / geo-primary): True active-active reduces RTO to sub-10 minutes for traffic routing, but achieving 15m RPO requires synchronous replication and higher cost (additional reserved capacity and higher outbound replication bandwidth).

We typically define an SLA boundary by region (region availability SLO + failover activation lead time). For contract language we can offer a regional continuity addendum that includes: defined activation runbook, pre-warm window guarantees, monthly reserved capacity commitment, and clearly enumerated SLA credit tiers for missed activation windows or RPO breaches.

I've looped in Karthik and Marissa to detail operational constraints and to draft a short addendum we can route to procurement. We'll propose concrete numbers and estimated cost delta in the next message.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-29T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calyx DR requirements: RTO/RPO targets and regional continuity

Team — quick operational note to include in the addendum draft:

1) Model preload time: for Calyx's largest fraud ensemble (approx 12B params across two submodels) cold load is ~10–12 minutes on p4d equivalent; however kv-cache (prefix history) rebuild varies with traffic shape and will likely need 15–35 minutes to reach steady-state for production latencies. Pre-warm (holding model residency + primed KV snapshot) reduces the KV rebuild window to 5–10 minutes.

2) Network failover: DNS/TCP routing cutover can be sub-minute with global load-balancer health checks, but fallback to a secondary region still requires session state alignment. We should require a 2-step acceptance test: (a) regional activation within X minutes under simulated failover, (b) RPO verified with transaction sampling.

3) Recommendation: propose 2-tier addendum lines — "Gold" (30m RTO / 15m RPO, reserved capacity + pre-warm, 20% premium on baseline committed spend) and "Silver" (60m RTO / 1h RPO, on-demand warm-up, 5% premium). Credit formula: sliding scale based on duration and frequency (e.g., first event <1% credit, repeat events escalate).

I'll draft the operational appendix with timings and acceptance test steps.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Eng — Redwood Inference

Samir —

Attached is a draft regional continuity addendum (v1). Highlights:

- Gold tier (recommended): commit to 30-minute activation RTO and 15-minute RPO for Calyx endpoints when Gold preconditions are met: (a) monthly reserved capacity at 2x baseline QPS, (b) pre-warm window within 24 hours of declared standby, and (c) streaming replication configured for transaction logs (we list supported connector patterns).
- Silver tier: 60-minute activation RTO and 1-hour RPO under on-demand warm-up; lower cost and faster onboarding.
- SLA credits (explicit):
  * Single activation event exceeding RTO but under 2x target: 5% monthly service credit.
  * Any event >2x target or repeat event within 30 days: 15% monthly service credit.
  * Three or more qualifying events in a rolling quarter: escalation clause with right to negotiate termination or additional credits.
- Acceptance test plan: staged failover simulation with traffic replay and a pass/fail criteria based on end-to-end latency and transaction delta thresholds. We propose joint test windows during onboarding and once-per-quarter re-validation.

Attachment: redwood-sla-addendum-v1.pdf (contains appendix with model preload timings, KV warm-up guidance, and runbook steps).

If this aligns, I can route the PDF to your procurement contact and include a DocuSign link. We've also included estimated pricing uplift per tier in the last page (Gold: +18–24% depending on bandwidth; Silver: +4–6%).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk procurement through the credit table.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
